turn_text: First off, I have a good relationship with Steve Scalise. I think you do a great job. I'll start a great relationship with Kevin McCarthy. So here's what I think is happening, and it's actually no different than when I ran against McConnell 11 months ago to be Republican leaders. The first conversation you ought to have is instead of about people, you should do it like you do in business. I'm a business guy. First you'd say, okay, so what are we looking for? What's the job description? And really what that means is how do we as a group want to be governed? And that's what they need to have a conversation. How do they want to be governed? What do they want to accomplish? And then it's probably relatively easier, or I don't know if it's easy, but then you can say, okay, so does that person fit the bill, right? And so that's the way we do it and visit. And that's what I think that's what we ought to be doing up here. We ought to say, this is what we're trying to accomplish. This is the way this is the way we are to be governed and what do we want? So my understanding is there's quite a few people that are going to put their name out there. I think I'm sold last night. They're going to ask you ready to make a presentation on Tuesday. And then I guess not a Wednesday. So I think there's going to be quite a few people that are going to put their names out there as an option. But it's really about how do you want to be government? And so there's a lot of them that the names are being flooded out there that I work with. I meet with house members every Wednesday night of do tonight here at my house in the MDC. to say how do we work together? In hearing what's great about what happens there, on Saturday, we actually work with the house to pass something. Now, both houses and it's failed by not passing any budget. That is a failure. That should have happened by September 30. So what's the next option? Say, okay, we're going to do this for a shorter period of time and have an absolute commitment to going through the budget. So we don't just have a rollout spending bill like we've done every year I've been up here. And that's a big, that's a big change. And so, you know, we're not where we need to be, but I'm optimistic that we're going to get there.

speaker: SPEAKER_04

turn_text: It's an exciting time. I mean, I think the country is saying something right now. They're saying, wait, if you talk to the American public, and I meet with people constantly, up here in Florida, they want a government that deals with inflation. They want a government that gets interest rates down. They want a government to make sure they've come up with their retirement. They want a government to get medical costs down. That's what they want out of their government. They don't want to be at war all the time. They want a government that's accountable. And I think what we're doing, and I think what's happening in these elections and what's happening after they get elected, they're saying, okay, How do we provide the public with what I told them I was going to do? And that's the fight we're having right now. It is hard. It's hard to balance the budget. I did it as governor. I thought I had to balance the budget in 20 years before I became governor. I did it. It's hard, right? We have to do that. If we want to get inflation to the control and we get interest rates down, you'd have to balance the budget. Well, that means you have to make choices. And what I've watched up here is people don't want to make a choice. They say, well, we're just going to take care of everybody. We're going to throw all the money out there. And that's why we're in position. We're in. This is a game changer. Take Schooner and McConnell. While they've been up here in leadership, the debt has gone from $5 to $3 trillion. The public is mad about that. And so it's filtered into how do we change things up here? We see is broken. And so I think the Republican Party, as long as we stand and fight for what we believe in, we're going to have a bright future. Now, if we become Democrat-like and don't say, well, I told you I want to bounce a budget, but I'm not really going to try, why would you elect somebody like that? So that's why I fight for, I fight for what I told people, I fight for a balanced budget. Is it hard? Yeah, but I'm going to fight for it every day and we're going to get there. I'm committed to get fiscal sanity to the federal government. That's what I ran on because I know that's better for every family in Florida.
